name: Euclid number
rephrased: A Euclid number is defined as the primorial of the nth prime number plus one.
implication_form: If n is a natural number, then the nth Euclid number is the primorial of the nth prime plus one.
explained: Euclid numbers (or Euclidean numbers) are a sequence of integers generated by multiplying the first n prime numbers and adding 1 (\(E_{n}=p_{n}\#+1\)), named for their role in proving the infinitude of primes, though they aren't always prime themselves, like \(E_{6}=30031=59\times 509\). They are closely related to the Euclid-Mullin sequence, a series of distinct primes where each new term is the smallest prime factor of the previous term plus one.
